claims.text: SPS of Mg-5Al-3Zn-2Sc-1Y at 920 °C for 30 minutes under 50 MPa and vacuum below 10^-3 Pa will produce a relative density greater than 98%.
The proposed treatment will produce an average grain size below 5 µm.
The resulting microstructure will be single-phase-like, consisting of an Mg-Sc-Y solid solution with fine Al-Zn precipitates.
Sc and Y additions form stable, fine Mg17Sc2 and Mg24Y5 intermetallic precipitates.
The Sc- and Y-containing precipitates pin grain boundaries.
Sc and Y suppress grain-boundary segregation of Mg and Zn.
Suppression of segregation promotes a homogeneous solid solution.
Sc and Y lower the effective sintering activation energy.
Sc and Y form transient grain-boundary liquid phases above 900 °C.
The transient liquid phases enhance mass transport and densification.
Grain-boundary segregation of Sc and Y inhibits unstable secondary-phase formation.
Sc and Y stabilize the surface oxide layer and thereby prevent Mg volatilization.
The proposed alloy will have an oxidation rate more than 50% lower than a standard-sintered Mg-Al-Zn alloy.
The proposed alloy will have a corrosion current density reduced by more than 60%.
Standard sintering of Mg-5Al-3Zn at 850 °C for one hour yields approximately 92% relative density.
Standard sintering of Mg-5Al-3Zn at 850 °C produces a multiphase microstructure with significant elemental segregation.
Sintering below 880 °C gives less than 95% relative density because diffusion is insufficient.
Temperatures above 950 °C cause more than 5% Mg loss.
Vacuum pressures above 10^-2 Pa cause more than 5% Mg loss.
Lower sintering temperatures produce unstable multiphase transformations that are avoided at 920 °C.

contradictions.description: The product is described as an Mg-Sc-Y solid solution containing fine Al-Zn precipitates, while the structural mediator additionally specifies Mg17Sc2 and Mg24Y5 intermetallic precipitates. Thus, the stated phase inventory is inconsistent or incomplete, and the meaning of 'single-phase-like' is unclear.

Sc and Y are said both to form stable intermetallic precipitates and to form transient liquid phases above 900 °C, but no sequence or phase-transformation pathway reconciles these two proposed states at the 920 °C hold.
